does_not_establish: that HS allowed or blocked anything; the relying party ran the function at its own door
that the agent is who it claims to be beyond what the presented signatures and keys on its own domain show

when a revocation without an anchor was issued, or that no revocation exists beyond those in revocations_seen; a revocation the principal signed is obeyed with or without an anchor, and its time is not proven until it is anchored
that the action was lawful, safe or wise; only that it was inside or outside the signed grant
that this record is a legal authorization or determines liability
that the immune rules stopped every harmful act; a clear verdict says only that no rule in the contract's immune terms fired on the request as presented, and the values it read are not in this record

that any content check ran, or that the same checks would answer the same way again; the record carries a salted commitment to the bytes the relying party says it sent to every runner (only a holder of the bytes and the salt can recompute it), the digest of each check it says it read, the identifiers of the rule sets, each decision and its marks, and nothing else about the content
that the rates measured for the named rule sets hold on this contract's scope; they were measured on the scopes of public datasets, not on a scope rendered from a contract
that the runners reached their answers apart from one another, or that their models, prompts or operators differ beyond the keys and rule set digests the record names
which runner's answer was right when the answers differ; disagreement_kind says only how they differ
why a runner gave no answer when its check says timeout or capped; those two are the relying party's own account, and no signed envelope shows them

that a pass here means what a pass means in a v0.4 record; a v0.4 block says pass for a check that answered pass with part of the content unread, while here such a runner is not counted as answered, so the block's decision may be null where v0.4 would say pass
establishes: that the relying party named here ran admit() over this contract, this action digest and this chain view, and signed the result
that the decision and reasons are what the shared clause evaluator (rules.evaluator_sha256) returns for those inputs; anyone holding them can recompute it
